column1: # Per-module memory caps for single-threaded (LEAN_NUM_THREADS=1) lean processes, in MiB of RssAnon.
#   peak_mib  the highest RssAnon seen for the module's lean process (sampled every 10 s, so a lower
#             bound) over two full single-threaded builds of the release base.
#   cap_mib   the cap the gate's memory watch enforces: the smallest tier of 4096 / 5120 / 6144 / 8192
#             at or above peak * 1.1; certificate modules keep the caps tools outside this file
#             already allow for them (cert_build-style builds, one at a time), so a few have less
#   mode      parallel  may build alongside other leans (cap 4096, the default)
#             solo      build alone (its imports first), only with enough MemAvailable
#             cert      certificate module: built alone through the certificate build wrapper
# Every cap is at most 6144 except WeakCore.TermStep (8192), which is approved only built alone,
# single-threaded, with at least 20 GiB of MemAvailable.
# The WeakCore peaks are from its current release.
# Every module whose peak is above 2500 MiB is listed; any other module gets the `*` row.
# A module killed at its cap gets one solo re-run at the next tier; killed again, the gate stops and
# the row must be re-measured and updated here (in the same commit as the change that grew it).
# The scc-blocks rows are Scc/Test/blocks.sh's per-program Lean checks of scc's AArch64 code output
# (.lake/scc-blocks/<prog>.arm.code.lean), run one at a time; peaks are the highest over five
# gate runs. Cap 6144 (under 10 % headroom for printidx and arith); why these checks need this much
